title: "Indicator Seasons" classification (Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter) for MACD-Histogram
description: A four-way classification from Elder ch. 32, purely informational, low-risk to add: combine MACD-Histogram's slope (already computed for Impulse) with its position relative to the centerline (also trivial) into one of Spring (rising, below centerline -- best time to go long), Summer (rising, above -- crowd-recognized uptrend, take profits on longs into strength), Autumn (falling, above -- best time to go short), Winter (falling, below -- crowd-recognized downtrend, cover shorts into weakness). This is a pure informational label on top of an already-computed series -- does not touch _determine_signal or confidence scoring.

checklist.step: Implement the 4-way season classification as a small pure function on the existing macd_histogram series.
Unit tests covering all four season transitions.
Expose as a new field on GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis (and indicator-history, for a historical season timeline); regenerate openapi.json/frontend types.
Document in docs/Analyse.md, explicitly noting this is informational only and not wired into signal logic.

decisions.decision: classify_season(histogram) lives in a new app/signals/seasons.py module and is exposed as a new `season` key inside the existing `indicators` dict/schema (AnalysisResponse.indicators.season, IndicatorHistoryPoint.season) rather than as a new top-level response field or under `screens`.
decisions.rationale: `season` is derived purely from the same macd_histogram series every other `indicators` entry (ema_13, macd_histogram, bull_power/bear_power, channel_upper/lower, rsi) is already keyed off of, and like rsi/channel bands it's computation+exposure-only, not a Screen/gate -- so it fits the existing `indicators` bucket's contract (informational, not read by _determine_signal/confidence) better than `screens` (which holds only the four Triple Screen/Impulse gate outputs `_determine_signal` actually reads) or a new top-level field (which every prior purely-informational addition -- rsi, channel_upper/lower -- avoided in favor of `indicators` already).

decisions.decision: Slope (rising/falling) reuses the same bar-over-bar "rising iff latest > previous, exact tie counts as falling" convention app.signals.impulse._direction already established, reimplemented locally in classify_season rather than importing the private `_direction` helper across modules.
decisions.rationale: Elder's book doesn't define a tie-breaking rule for "is the indicator rising or falling" -- reusing the existing, already-rationale'd convention (a not-yet-advanced value hasn't demonstrated rising momentum) keeps every 'rising/falling' comparison in app/signals/ consistent rather than inventing a second, competing tie-break rule for the same kind of question. Reimplemented rather than imported: app.signals.confidence.score_elder_ray_confirmation already set this precedent (its own docstring explicitly says it "reuses the same ... convention as app.signals.impulse._direction" while reimplementing the comparison itself, rather than importing the underscore-prefixed helper across module boundaries) -- classify_season follows that same established pattern instead of introducing cross-module imports of a private function, which would also require exporting _direction as a public API it currently isn't.

decisions.decision: Position relative to the centerline treats an exact histogram value of 0 as "below" the centerline, not "above" -- i.e. `above_centerline = latest > 0` (strict), so latest == 0 falls into Spring/Winter, never Summer/Autumn.
decisions.rationale: Elder ch. 32 doesn't address the zero-exactly case explicitly (a near-impossible float value in practice, but the function needs a defined answer). Chose consistency with the existing sign-convention precedent in app.signals.triple_screen._is_force_index_spike, which treats `sign * latest <= 0` as "wrong sign" -- i.e. a reading of exactly zero is never treated as satisfying a directional (positive or negative) condition in this codebase's existing MACD/Force-Index-adjacent sign checks. The alternative (treating 0 as "above") was rejected only because it would introduce a second, inconsistent zero-handling rule alongside that existing precedent for no compensating benefit -- Elder's own text gives no reason to prefer one over the other at this exact boundary.

decisions.decision: classify_season returns None (mapped to a nullable `season` field) only when fewer than 2 histogram points are available (or either of the last two is NaN) -- not for any other 'thin data' condition.
decisions.rationale: A slope needs at least two points to exist at all -- this is the minimum-possible warm-up (shorter than rsi's 9-day window or the Autoenvelope channel's ~100-bar window), so nullability follows the same established 'not enough history yet -> null, not a fabricated value' convention those two already use in the Indicators/IndicatorHistoryPoint schemas, just triggered by a much shorter and rarer condition (effectively only the very first daily bar of any real history).
